name: Salzburg
tagline: Salt, prince-archbishops and a child called Mozart
intro: Salzburg means 'salt castle'. Salt made it rich, and for centuries its prince-archbishops ruled it like kings — building a fortress, a Baroque cathedral and gardens fit for a palace. Then a boy was born on Getreidegasse and the city found its soundtrack.

lessons.title: The yellow house
lessons.hook: Walk down Getreidegasse, a narrow lane of wrought-iron shop signs, to number 9.
lessons.challenge: What colour is the front of the house where Mozart was born?
lessons.rubric: Correct if the player says yellow.
hints: Stand back across the lane and look up.
lessons.story: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born here on 27 January 1756, in the family's flat on the third floor, where the Mozarts lived for 26 years. As a small child he toured Europe as a prodigy with his sister Nannerl. The house has been a museum since the 1880s.

lessons.title: Three dates on the gates
lessons.hook: Stand in front of the cathedral and look at the three iron gates in its marble front. Each one carries a year.
lessons.challenge: The years mark the times the cathedral was consecrated. Which is the oldest?
hints: Read the numbers on the wrought-iron gates.
lessons.story: A cathedral has stood here since the 8th century; the first was consecrated in 774. After a fire, Prince-Archbishop Paris Lodron consecrated the Baroque cathedral you see in 1628. A bomb hit the dome in 1944, and the restored cathedral was consecrated again in 1959. Mozart was baptised here the day after he was born.

lessons.title: A palace built for love
lessons.hook: Walk into the Mirabell Gardens and find the fountain with a winged horse rearing up in the middle.
lessons.challenge: Which winged horse from Greek myth is the statue?
lessons.rubric: Correct if the player says Pegasus.
hints: A winged horse from Greek myth.
lessons.story: Prince-Archbishop Wolf Dietrich von Raitenau built this palace around 1606 for Salome Alt, the woman he loved and the mother of his many children — around fifteen. When he fell from power in 1612, his successor threw her out and renamed the palace Mirabell: 'wonderful and beautiful'. The copper Pegasus dates from 1661. In The Sound of Music, Maria and the children dance around it singing 'Do-Re-Mi'.

lessons.title: The castle nobody took
lessons.hook: Look up — or ride the funicular — to the white fortress on the Festungsberg that watches over the whole city.
lessons.challenge: Building began during a power struggle between the Pope and the Emperor. In which century?
lessons.rubric: Correct if the player says the 11th century (1077).
lessons.story: Archbishop Gebhard began the fortress in 1077, in the middle of the Investiture Controversy: he had sided with the Pope against Emperor Henry IV and needed protection. His successors kept building, and it grew into one of the largest medieval castles in Europe. In the Peasants' War of 1525 it was besieged for weeks, but never taken.

lessons.title: Caves in the cliff
lessons.hook: Walk into St Peter's cemetery, between the wrought-iron graves, to the rock wall of the Mönchsberg. Look up at the openings in the cliff.
lessons.challenge: What has been carved into the cliff above the cemetery?
lessons.rubric: Correct if the player says catacombs / caves / chapels cut into the rock.
hints: There are doors, windows and stairs in the rock.
The sign at the entrance calls them 'Katakomben'.
lessons.story: St Rupert founded St Peter's Abbey around 696, making it the oldest monastery in the German-speaking world with an unbroken history. The 'catacombs' cut into the rock above the cemetery were probably not tombs at all, but early Christian places to meet and pray. The cemetery also inspired a scene in The Sound of Music.

lessons.title: A man on a golden ball
lessons.hook: On Kapitelplatz, beside the cathedral, a huge golden ball sits on the cobblestones.
lessons.challenge: What is standing on top of the golden ball?
lessons.rubric: Correct if the player says a man / a person / a figure.
hints: Look right up at the top.
He's wearing a white shirt and black trousers.
lessons.story: Sphaera, by German sculptor Stephan Balkenhol, arrived in 2007 as part of Salzburg's Walk of Modern Art: an ordinary man in a white shirt and black trousers, standing calmly on a giant golden sphere. Balkenhol leaves the meaning open — in a city of prince-archbishops and Baroque saints, he's simply a person looking out over the square.
